thread:
alex: FYI — customer complains console export (CSV) strips out kms_encrypted fields even though viewer can see them in the UI. Happens on 30d+ exports. Anyone seen this?
caroline: Ugh. I remember a tokenization/encoding issue with CSV streaming. But stripping KMS fields sounds like an RBAC check at export time. :thinking_face:
nate: Do we have logs for the export job id? audit-bot: export_job_started id=exp_20260312_79f
alex: they sent the job id: exp_20260312_79f. It shows success in UI but downloaded CSV has empty "kms_key_id" and "encrypted_blob" columns for ~40% of rows.
maria: Could be lazy redaction during stream if the exporter can't call KMS.Decrypt. That would mean the read path uses user role instead of service principal.
caroline: Right — console export should use the backend service identity with kms:Decrypt for export processing, not the UI user role. If there's a permission check mapping bug, audit_viewer won't get export-decrypt rights.
nate: I pulled the job log:
```
[INFO] export_job exp_20260312_79f started by user: alice@customer.com
[INFO] opening stream, role=service/export-worker
ERROR: http 403 KMS.Decrypt denied for principal arn:aws:iam::12345:role/audit_viewer
[WARN] falling back to redaction for 432 rows
[INFO] job completed: status=partial_success, rows=1200, redacted=432
```
alex: Here’s the schema the customer expects (CSV headers): `timestamp,actor,action,resource,ip,user_agent,kms_key_id,encrypted_blob,metadata`
maria: We should validate exports against the audit event schema server-side and fail-fast if required fields are redacted when the user requested full export. For customers with restricted KMS we can present a clear error: "Export failed: missing KMS permissions" instead of silent redaction.
caroline: Agreed. Also need to consider pagination/time-window sampling. Large exports currently stream everything and hit KMS rate limits. We should chunk the export and surface progress with job ids.
nate: Proposal: 1) change exporter to always use service/export-worker identity for decryption, 2) add a new RBAC permission `audit.export_decrypt` that maps to service flow, 3) add export validation step to fail if >1% rows redacted unless user explicitly chose redaction.
alex: +1 on the validation. Also add JSON newline-stream export as fallback — that avoids CSV encoding quirks for binary blobs.
maria: Implementation notes: we'll need a migration to the audit schema: add boolean `encrypted_blob_present` and `redacted_reason` fields to make redaction visible in exports. Also add unit tests for the `export_worker` role KMS call path.
caroline: UX asks: surface export permission in console: disable CSV/JSON buttons with tooltip "missing export permissions" and link to docs/privileges. Also add an audit export preview (first 100 rows) where fields are shown with redaction markers.
nate: Filed infra ticket infra#8423 to add service role policy with kms:Decrypt on audit KMS keys and to rotate key alias for testing.
alex: I'll open a security PR for the RBAC change + validation logic. Patch will include: policy change, exporter role switch, export job validation, and tests. Tentative PR: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/12046
maria: QA plan: 1) create a test key with deny for audit_viewer, 2) run 10k-row export, ensure redaction only occurs when intended, 3) validate JSON newline and CSV outputs match schema, 4) test UI disable/tooltip.
caroline: Can someone add an integration test that replays historical events (some KMS-encrypted, some not) to the export job? I'd like to catch streaming edgecases.
alex: @nate can you take the export_worker + KMS policy change? @maria take tests & schema change. I'll do the console UX and PR.
audit-bot: export_job_update id=exp_20260312_79f status=partial_success redacted=432
caroline: Thanks. Filing a follow-up to add explicit error messages rather than silent redaction. I'll put an RFC on the security board for the RBAC model for exports. :thumbsup:
